messages:
ashley_support: SEV1 - Acme Inc reports intermittent 502 / TLS handshake errors hitting api.redwood.com over their AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) via TGW. Started ~09:05 UTC, ~10% of requests failing. Sample error: "tls: handshake failure". Any ideas?

mike_network: Can you grab a few things from them: endpoint id + ENI IPs, SG on the endpoint, route tables for the subnets, whether Private DNS is enabled, and a dig/traceroute/tcpdump from a failing client?

ashley_support: Pasted what they sent:
```
# dig tests
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @10.100.0.5
10.10.5.12
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
54.23.12.34
```
They also ran `traceroute` showing path via their FW -> TGW -> spoke -> endpoint ENI. tcpdump shows ClientHello to both 10.10.5.12 and 54.23.12.34 intermittently.

mike_network: That's classic split-horizon / resolver caching. If some hosts hit corporate DNS cache or public resolvers they'll get the public A record. PrivateLink only works if clients resolve to the endpoint IP. Ask them: what's /etc/resolv.conf on the failing host and dhcp option set for VPC? Also check their dnsmasq/forwarders.

ashley_support: They replied: VPC had DHCP pointing at 10.100.0.5 (mgmt resolver). But their on-prem DNSmasq caches and conditionally forwards. TTL was 60s but cache had older public entries. Their firewall also blocks egress to our public edge IPs (so when resolution hits public IP, connection can't complete). They ran these repro steps for us:
```
1) dig +short api.redwood.com @10.100.0.5 -> 10.10.5.12
2) dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8 -> 54.23.12.34
3) curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.com:443:10.10.5.12' https://api.redwood.com/health -> OK
4) curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health -> intermittently TLS handshake timeout
```

mike_network: Root cause: split-horizon DNS + caching -> some requests go to our public edge but their firewall blocks those IPs -> TLS handshake fails / 502s. Fix we recommended:
- enable Private DNS on the interface endpoint (if not already)
- ensure corporate DNS forwards queries for api.redwood.com (or *.redwoodapi domain) to the VPC resolver via Route53 Resolver outbound/inbound endpoints or conditional forwarders
- flush dnsmasq caches and restart resolver on affected hosts
- as a safety, allow egress to our public IP ranges (if they plan to use public fallback)

jordan_csm: Customer applied fixes: turned Private DNS on, added conditional forwarders to VPC resolver, flushed caches, and opened egress to our edge IPs temporarily. They report error rate dropped to 0 and latency stable.

ashley_support: I'll follow up in 24h to confirm stability and close ticket. Adding KB link: https://redwood.internal.kb/vpce-dns-fallback (internal).
